Her offer of freedom is a tool of control, and her knowledge of the party’s actions implies surveillance.

Their existence is denied publicly but suspected by those who remember the city’s former stability.

subject: Deepking’s Court

subject: Droki
fact: Droki is a Duergar living in the West Cleft District among the Derro. He is the suspected linchpin of a conspiracy linking the Council of Savants and Clan Lairds to corruption in Gracklstugh. Though not yet encountered, his existence is the focus of Errde’s investigation. His actions have triggered a city-wide unraveling of law and order, and his capture is the key to exposing the Deepking’s court.

subject: Droki
fact: Droki is the key figure linked to the Council of Savants and possibly the Clan Lairds, whose involvement in corruption is central to Errde’s investigation and the reward structure.
source_quote: Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption. He is linked to the Council of Savants and maybe even elements of the Clan Lairds.

subject: Droki
fact: I have been tracking a particular Duergar named Droki. He lives in the West Cleft District, where the Derro live.
source_quote: I have been tracking a particular Duergar named Droki. He lives in the West Cleft District, where the Derro live.

subject: Drow
fact: The Drow is from Menzoberranzan and views Duergar violence as crude and styleless. He contrasts his people’s artful treachery with the Duergar’s brutal efficiency, expressing disdain for their lack of finesse.

subject: Drow
fact: The Drow sitting next to the Halfling splutters, "Look, friend, I am from Menzoberranzan. The backstabbing and politicking are nothing compared to the Duergar. I mean, we will do it with style and finesse. Here, it’s just slaughter. No torture, no speeches, no art, and I mean no style. It was just a brutal struggle. They just engage in violence for violence’s sake. It’s disgraceful if you ask me."
source_quote: Look, friend, I am from Menzoberranzan. The backstabbing and politicking are nothing compared to the Duergar. I mean, we will do it with style and finesse. Here, it’s just slaughter. No torture, no speeches, no art, and I mean no style. It was just a brutal struggle. They just engage in violence for violence’s sake. It’s disgraceful if you ask me.

subject: Duergar patrol
fact: A patrol of Duergar responded to Thorin’s inquiry about aberrant behavior by confirming increased incidents of non-compliant, self-destructive actions among stone giants. They stated the militias’ workload had risen and that no underlying cause was known, though clan leaders might withhold information.
source_quote: We have noticed that there have been significantly more incidents of this kind of behavior. As a result, the work of the militias has increased.

subject: Errde
fact: Errde is a city protector linked to the Deepking’s court, offering rewards for uncovering corruption tied to Droki, the Council of Savants, and the Clan Lairds. She controls access to freedom and armory resources.
source_quote: Errde smiles, "You have found me proof!" ... "And I can offer one more thing."

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull is captain of the Stone Guards on the lake. She uses indirect methods to recruit outsiders to find Droki, avoiding direct confrontation with the Derro. She presents requests as friendly inquiries but maintains authority.

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde Blackskull says, "There is something very wrong going on in my city. Some kind of corruption eats at the heart of the Deepking’s court. Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption. He is linked to the Council of Savants and maybe even elements of the Clan Lairds. Discovery of this conspiracy will earn me great favor with the Deepking. And when that happens, I swear you will get free and safe passage out of the city."
source_quote: There is something very wrong going on in my city. Some kind of corruption eats at the heart of the Deepking’s court. Droki is the key to uncovering that corruption. He is linked to the Council of Savants and maybe even elements of the Clan Lairds. Discovery of this conspiracy will earn me great favor with the Deepking. And when that happens, I swear you will get free and safe passage out of the city.

subject: Errde Blackskull
fact: Errde is the captain of the Stone Guards and an agent of the Overlake Hold. She is pragmatic, emotionally controlled, and deeply invested in uncovering corruption tied to Droki and the Council of Savants. She offers the party financial reward and protection from Drow slave-hunters in exchange for intelligence. Her offer is laced with manipulation — she presents herself as the only guarantor of the party’s freedom, while concealing her own ties to the Deepking’s court.

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn is the Custodian of the Flame, the chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who tend to Themberchaud’s needs.
source_quote: I am the Custodian of the Flame, the chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who tend to Themberchaud’s needs.

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn, Custodian of the Flame and chief of the Keepers of the Flame, approached Zalthir and offered him safe passage through Gracklstugh in exchange for service. He used a badge to command other Duergar, referenced the fire dragon Themberchaud, and made a final threat that refusal would result in hostility. He laughed at jokes and was literal-minded.
source_quote: Gartokkar laughs. “ A joke. I have not heard a good joke in so long.”

subject: Gartokkar Xundorn
fact: Gartokkar is the Custodian of the Flame and chief of the Keepers of the Flame in Gracklstugh. He is literal, humorless, and proud of his role maintaining the city’s furnaces through a captive red dragon. He offers Daz and his party safe passage in exchange for service, but his offer expires tomorrow. He is a key figure in the city’s power structure and is aware of the dragon’s inevitable fate — replacement through murder.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is a sneaky observer who gathers intelligence by peeking into restricted areas. He is instrumental in uncovering hidden truths about the Darklake Brewery and the Keepers of the Flame.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum is an orc who witnessed the death of a two-headed stone giant, observed the Duergar's flame device, and chose to intervene in the battle with his mace. He is attentive to subtle behavioral cues, such as Daz’s deliberate weakening of spells and Thorin’s prayers for the dead. He is currently navigating factional politics in Gracklstugh with caution.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum notices that the fire comes from a device they are holding. It is a tube that connects to a bottle on their back. At the front of the tube, a small flame sits outside the tube. He realizes that the flame is produced from some kind of magic concoction lit by the tiny flame when the duergar operator pulls a lever.
source_quote: Grygum notices that the fire comes from a device they are holding. It is a tube that connects to a bottle on their back. At the front of the tube, a small flame sits outside the tube. He realizes that the flame is produced from some kind of magic concoction lit by the tiny flame when the duergar operator pulls a lever.

subject: Grygum
fact: Grygum witnessed the death of a two-headed stone giant at the hands of Duergar, observed Daz deliberately weakening his magic, and chose to intervene with his mace after hearing Zalthir's fists and Thorin's blade strike the giant. He later saw the Duergar shrink to standard size after the giant's death and watched Thorin pray for the dead.
source_quote: Grygum looks at Daz, and then looks at the giant, and thinks, “Well, I guess Daz chose to weaken his spell purposely.”

subject: Halfling
fact: The Halfling is an outsider who survives by appearing non-threatening. He knows much about the Deepking’s madness, the Keepers of the Flame, and the Gray Ghosts, but refuses to be drawn into the game. He speaks in riddles and avoids commitment.

subject: Halfling
fact: The halfling whispers, "You must have met the Keepers of the Flame? They are in a pickle, what with the Gray Ghosts and the Crown."
source_quote: You must have met the Keepers of the Flame? They are in a pickle, what with the Gray Ghosts and the Crown.

subject: Hgraam
fact: We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam.
source_quote: We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam.

subject: Rihuud
fact: I am Dorhun, and this is Rihuud. We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam.
source_quote: I am Dorhun, and this is Rihuud. We were both apprentices to Stonespeaker Hgraam.

subject: Rihuud
fact: Rihuud is Dorhun’s companion, also an apprentice to Stonespeaker Hgraam. He is silent, observant, and present during the conversation with Thorin. Though he speaks little, his presence reinforces the stone giants’ collective grief and their institutional role in maintaining order. He may hold unspoken knowledge about the corruption in Gracklstugh.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin attempted to subdue the two-headed stone giant but was overruled by the Duergar, who killed it. He later questioned Duergar about aberrant behavior in the city, learned of increased militia activity due to similar incidents, and was approached by Dorhun and Rihuud, two stone giant apprentices of Stonespeaker Hgraam. He was invited to visit Cairngorm Cavern and granted safe passage by the Stone Guards.
source_quote: Thorin breathes a sigh of relief, “Yes.”

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin believes Stone Giants don’t move and are taciturn to a fault.
source_quote: Although Thorin is unfamiliar with the patterns of behavior of the Duergar, the madness of a stone giant is unheard of. The Stone Giants don’t move. They are taciturn to a fault.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a dwarf who seeks to understand the nature of madness in stone giants and Duergar behavior. He is deeply moral, reluctant to kill, and emotionally affected by the giant’s death. He is being courted by multiple factions — Stone Guards, Keepers of the Flame, and possibly the Deepking’s court — and is torn between loyalty to giants and survival in a corrupt city. He values clarity of intent and is wary of hidden agendas.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin is a wary adventurer who is tempted to ally with the Stone Guards but is deterred by the Halfling’s warnings. He struggles to distinguish whether he is helping the city or the faction, and seeks clarity before committing.

subject: Thorin
fact: Thorin remembers that the Duergars are literal people but is uncertain how to continue.
source_quote: Thorin remembers that the Duergars are literal people but is uncertain how to continue.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir encountered Gartokkar Xundorn, Custodian of the Flame and chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who offered him safe passage through Gracklstugh in exchange for service. He noted Gartokkar’s non-self-inflicted ear notches, observed the Duergar’s authority via a badge, and was told the Keepers use a fire dragon to heat Gracklstugh’s furnaces. The offer expired tomorrow, and refusal would mean future hostility.
source_quote: Gartokkar is a Duergar, and he is literal and misses the sarcasm, “Yes. The Keepers of the Flame tend to the dragon’s needs.”

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir immediately notices the scars on his ears, four notches that don’t look self-inflicted.
source_quote: Zalthir immediately notices the scars on his ears, four notches that don’t look self-inflicted.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is a character who prioritizes self-preservation and is intrigued by power. He is approached by Gartokkar, Custodian of the Flame, who offers him safe passage in exchange for service. Zalthir recognizes the value of influence and is drawn to the authority Gartokkar wields. He is currently considering the offer before its expiration, aware that refusal may lead to hostility.

subject: Zalthir
fact: Zalthir is trying hard to protect himself from being burned alive, crushed by a giant, or arrested.
source_quote: Zalthir is trying hard to protect himself from being burned alive, crushed by a giant, or arrested.

subject: 175 gold pieces of equipment
fact: A reward of 175 gold pieces in equipment from the armory is offered by Errde upon provision of Droki and proof; a second 175 gold pieces is promised upon delivery.
source_quote: I offer you 175 gold pieces of equipment from our armory. ... I will give you 175 more.

subject: 175 gold pieces of equipment
fact: Errde offers 175 gold pieces of equipment as partial payment for the mission. The equipment is drawn from the Overlake Hold armory — likely superior Duergar-made gear. It is both reward and trap: it binds the party to her cause, and its value makes them targets. Accepting it is an act of allegiance.

subject: 175 gold pieces of equipment
fact: I offer you 175 gold pieces of equipment from our armory.
source_quote: I offer you 175 gold pieces of equipment from our armory.

subject: badge
fact: A device flashed by Gartokkar to command other Duergar to disperse. It demonstrated his authority over the patrol and implied a system of rank or command within the Keepers of the Flame.
source_quote: Gartokkar flashes a bade of some kind, and the other Duergar move away quickly.

subject: Darklake Brewery Stout
fact: The Stout is a thick, dark beverage served in the Overlake Hold. It is consumed by Thorin and others as a symbol of temporary camaraderie, but its flavor is overshadowed by the tension of political maneuvering.

subject: dragon horde value
fact: The Keepers of the Flame give the fire dragon a horde and pamper it, but must kill and replace it when it becomes too powerful.
source_quote: The keepers of the flame give him a horde, and they pamper him... the Keepers must kill and replace the dragon with a new one

subject: Droki’s evidence
fact: The evidence Errde seeks regarding Droki is not yet seen, but it is implied to be documentation, magical residue, or testimony linking him to the Council of Savants and Clan Lairds. It is the key to exposing the corruption at the heart of the Deepking’s court. Whoever holds it holds the power to change Gracklstugh — or destroy it.

subject: flame device
fact: A tube connected to a bottle on the back of a Duergar, producing a flame at its tip when a lever is pulled. Used to kill the two-headed stone giant. Grygum observed it as a magic concoction lit by a tiny flame.
source_quote: It is a tube that connects to a bottle on their back. At the front of the tube, a small flame sits outside the tube.

subject: flame device
fact: The flame device is a Duergar invention: a tube connected to a bottle on the back, producing a controlled flame from a magic concoction lit by a tiny flame. It is used to kill stone giants. It represents the fusion of alchemy, engineering, and forbidden magic in Gracklstugh. Its existence suggests the Duergar have developed weapons capable of overcoming even ancient giants.

subject: freedom guarantee value
fact: Errde can guarantee freedom from Drow slave-hunters by denying their presence in the city.
source_quote: If a particular group of Drow were to come looking for some escaped slaves, I could tell them that they are not here.

subject: Gartokkar’s badge
fact: Gartokkar’s badge is a symbol of authority among the Keepers of the Flame. When flashed, it causes other Duergar to retreat instantly. It is a tool of control, likely enchanted or culturally sacred. It confirms his status as a high-ranking official and reveals the hierarchical nature of the Keepers of the Flame.

subject: Gracklstugh
fact: The furnaces of Gracklstugh must be kept hot, and instead of using a large amount of kindling, we use a fire dragon that burns stone hot that then is used to keep the furnaces running.
source_quote: The furnaces of Gracklstugh must be kept hot, and instead of using a large amount of kindling, we use a fire dragon that burns stone hot that then is used to keep the furnaces running.

subject: Pastries and warm liquid
fact: A subordinate brings some pastries and some warm liquid to drink.
source_quote: A subordinate brings some pastries and some warm liquid to drink.

subject: Pastries and warm liquid
fact: Served during the meeting in the Overlake Hold, these items are acts of ritual hospitality meant to soften the authority of the Stone Guards. Their simplicity reflects the region’s austerity.

subject: silver candlestick value
fact: The Keepers of the Flame receive 175 gold pieces of equipment as reward, with another 175 promised upon completion.
source_quote: I offer you 175 gold pieces of equipment from our armory... I will give you 175 more

subject: stone weapons
fact: Curious weapons carried by the Duergar accompanying Dorhun and Rihuud. They were distinct from standard arms and suggested a specialized role, possibly ceremonial or defensive, in the interaction between Duergar and stone giants.
source_quote: flanked by Duergar, armed with curious stone weapons.

subject: Stone weapons
fact: Duergar, armed with curious stone weapons.
source_quote: Duergar, armed with curious stone weapons.

subject: Stone weapons
fact: The Stone Guards wield crude, heavy stone weapons, symbolizing their connection to the Stone Giants and their rejection of refined or magical tools. These weapons are feared for their blunt, unyielding force.

subject: stone weapons
fact: The stone weapons carried by the Stone Guards and Dorhun’s escort are unusual — not just tools of war, but symbols of authority. They are likely enchanted, possibly bonded to the giants’ will. They are used to enforce order and are feared by Duergar. Their presence signals that the stone giants still hold residual power in the city.

subject: stone weapon value
fact: The Stone Guards carry curious stone weapons, and their permission is required to enter the city.
source_quote: Stone Guards, you are to let them through

subject: Themberchaud
fact: Gartokkar Xundorn is the Custodian of the Flame, the chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who tend to Themberchaud’s needs.
source_quote: Gartokkar Xundorn is the Custodian of the Flame, the chief of the Keepers of the Flame, who tend to Themberchaud’s needs.

subject: Tube and bottle device
fact: It is a tube that connects to a bottle on their back. At the front of the tube, a small flame sits outside the tube. He realizes that the flame is produced from some kind of magic concoction lit by the tiny flame when the duergar operator pulls a lever.
source_quote: It is a tube that connects to a bottle on their back. At the front of the tube, a small flame sits outside the tube. He realizes that the flame is produced from some kind of magic concoction lit by the tiny flame when the duergar operator pulls a lever.

subject: Cairngorm Cavern meeting
fact: Dorhun has invited the party to Cairngorm Cavern, a location tied to the old stonespeakers and the memory of Hgraam. This meeting may reveal the origins of the Deepking’s madness, the truth about the stone giants’ immunity, or a hidden prophecy. It is a potential turning point — a chance to align with ancient wisdom or be trapped by it.

subject: Daz's allegiance
fact: Daz is considering whether to join a faction, but his final decision is not stated.
source_quote: At this point, Daz wonders if they should interview the various factions to find out which one they should join or whether they should join any of them.

subject: Dorhun’s invitation to Cairngorm Cavern
fact: Dorhun’s invitation to Thorin, after confirming Hgraam’s death, implies hidden knowledge or a ritual to be performed. The cavern may hold clues to the stone giant aberrations or the fate of the Stonespeaker.
source_quote: Did you kill him?

subject: Dragon egg procurement
fact: The possibility of purchasing and hatching dragon eggs is known, suggesting an alternative to the Keepers’ cycle of killing and replacing dragons. This raises the question of whether the system can be subverted or outsourced.

subject: Droki’s conspiracy
fact: Droki is the key to exposing corruption in Gracklstugh. He is linked to the Council of Savants and Clan Lairds, and his capture may reveal who is manipulating the Deepking. The party must decide whether to pursue him for the Stone Guards, for themselves, or to expose the conspiracy to the city. His fate will determine the balance of power in Gracklstugh.

subject: Droki's corruption
fact: The full extent of Droki’s corruption and his links to the Council of Savants and Clan Lairds is not fully revealed.
source_quote: Droki is linked to the Council of Savants and maybe even elements of the Clan Lairds.

subject: escaped slaves
fact: The whereabouts of escaped slaves and the potential arrival of Drow seeking them remain an unresolved plot thread, with Errde holding the power to conceal their location.
source_quote: If a particular group of Drow were to come looking for some escaped slaves, I could tell them that they are not here.

subject: Gartokkar’s true motives
fact: Gartokkar’s sudden offer to Zalthir, his emphasis on ‘service,’ and his threat of future hostility suggest an agenda beyond mere recruitment. His laughter at jokes and emotional openness may be a calculated facade.
source_quote: The offer expires tomorrow. And if you don’t accept the offer, I cannot promise we will be so friendly when we meet next.

subject: mystery of the stone giant aberrations
fact: Multiple stone giants have exhibited non-compliant, self-destructive behavior, causing increased militia activity. No cause is known, though clan leaders may be withholding information. The phenomenon appears linked to the death of Stonespeaker Hgraam and the arrival of new giants.
source_quote: We have noticed that there have been significantly more incidents of this kind of behavior... And we know of no underlying cause.

subject: nature of corruption
fact: The definition and manifestation of corruption are contested and evolving — framed as market rule-breaking, grift, chaos, and destruction — with no consensus among the characters.
source_quote: Things were not proceeding according to the rules of the market, of the bazaar. It starts with not obeying the rules. Then it proceeds to grift, then chaos, and then destruction.

subject: the Deepking’s madness
fact: The Deepking’s sudden detachment from reality is the root cause of Gracklstugh’s collapse. Laws are arbitrary, corruption is systemic, and factions are turning on each other. The party must uncover whether this madness is natural, magical, or engineered — and who, if anyone, is controlling it. The answer may determine whether the city can be saved — or must be destroyed.

subject: The Deepking's madness
fact: The cause of the Deepking’s madness is unexplained and unresolved.
source_quote: It all began with the Deepking’s madness.

subject: The Keepers' vulnerability
fact: The Keepers of the Flame are in a 'pickle' with the Gray Ghosts and the Crown. Their control over the Red Dragon is not absolute, and their methods may be unsustainable. Their long-term survival is uncertain.

subject: Themberchaud’s origin and control
fact: The fire dragon Themberchaud is central to Gracklstugh’s infrastructure, but its origin, nature, and the full extent of the Keepers’ control over it remain unexplained. Its use of stone as fuel and its apparent sentience suggest deeper magical or divine ties.
source_quote: We use a fire dragon that burns stone hot...

subject: the party’s allegiance
fact: The party is being courted by multiple factions: Stone Guards, Keepers of the Flame, and possibly the Deepking’s court. Each offers power, protection, or wealth — but at a cost. The party must decide whether to serve the city, survive it, or overthrow it. Their choice will determine whether they become players in the game — or remain outsiders, like the halfling.

subject: the red dragon’s fate
fact: The red dragon used to fuel Gracklstugh’s furnaces is kept alive only through pampering and a false hoard. The Keepers of the Flame must kill and replace it when it becomes too powerful or realizes it is not in charge. The party must decide whether to protect the dragon, sabotage the Keepers, or exploit its eventual death for their own gain.

subject: The Red Dragon's origin
fact: How the Red Dragon came to serve as a furnace-lighter is unexplained.
source_quote: The red dragon keeps the stones hot enough for the furnaces to burn.

subject: Thorin's home
fact: Thorin wants to understand the nature of Stone Giants, but his own origins or motivations for seeking them are not specified.
source_quote: Thorin explains his curious relationship with giants and how he got here.

subject: Which faction to join?
fact: Daz and Thorin are undecided about whether to join any faction. They are wary of being drawn into the game, but the need for purpose and survival forces them to consider alliances. The Halfling’s warnings complicate their decision.

subject: Zalthir's future
fact: Zalthir’s decision about whether to accept Gartokkar’s offer is unresolved.
source_quote: The offer expires tomorrow. And if you don’t accept the offer, I cannot promise we will be so friendly when we meet next.
